items.note: Two preregistered experiments (N = 2,582 combined, split not stated) expose writers to biased AI autocomplete versus static text and measure post-task attitudes; no creativity or diversity outcome on the written text in the abstract. Same study as PsyArXiv 10.31234/osf.io/mhjn6.

Designers ideate with ChatGPT-4 and DALL-E versus traditional sketching, and creativity scores are compared with independent-samples t-tests; assignment and N not stated, and the sample is designers already experienced with AI.

CHI system paper: within-subjects study (N = 12) of InkIdeator versus a baseline without dimensional keywords; outcomes look like perceived ideation support, and N is far below 50. Same as arXiv 2601.18193.

Generative AI's effect on design creativity under the 4P model; a modified Consensual Assessment Technique rates products (AI supports effectiveness, lowers originality), but the comparison design and N are not stated.

45 industrial design undergraduates divided into no tool, Pinterest search, or Midjourney; 10 experts rate originality, effectiveness, usability, and feasibility. The abstract says 'divided', not random, and N is below 50.

Multi-wave field study in two companies plus an online experiment on personal-life AI-assisted creating and workplace creativity; conference abstract only, the manipulation and creativity measure (possibly self- or supervisor-rated) are unclear.

Mixed-design experiment (N = 905) with human versus hybrid triads that include an undisclosed supportive or contrarian AI teammate on analytical, creative, and ethical tasks; reported outcomes are psychological safety and discussion quality, so likely out unless creative-task output is scored in the full text.

UIST system paper: between-subject user study of XCreation (generative cross-modal picture-book tool) versus a comparison condition; creativity, controllability, and usability may be self-reported, and N is not stated.

Master's thesis (UvA): 40 participants write stories alone, with a human partner, and with GPT-5.1, scored for semantic diversity, novelty, and surprise; abstract not reachable (event page 404, only search snippets), and N is below 50.
12 design master's students ideate with Midjourney versus Pinterest; think-aloud and interview process analysis, with 'more unique design solutions' possibly not formally scored; N far below 50.
